items.title: 52060_Eddie Barefield oral history interview
items.q: And they beat Buddy Rich up down there for trying to come and hear -- trying to hear Lucky Millinder's band. Lucky played there in the colored section.

ctx.x: From what I hear. Not until, you know, the late '30s and before the war -- that it started changing somewhat. You know, even then you'd go down 52nd Street, you know. You could play, but you don't mix with the people or --

Well, in fact, in Florida you couldn't even play for a white dance in Florida. I remember when I was there with Ella, when I went to Florida, Chauncey Horton drew $50.00, he sent home and went down to the telegraph station. I get a call to come down there and rescue him because he had too much money. And they wanted to know where this guy got $50.00 at.

And I had to go and get him. He had sent money home to his wife, you know. And it was rough. In fact, they beat Buddy Rich up down there for trying to come and hear -- trying to hear Lucky Millinder's band. Lucky played there in the colored section.
